quote: That is quite high, so we'll definitely help get that cut down for you.
stewart_read: Rep captured the bill range but only weakly acknowledged pain ('quite high') without flipping it into alignment-against-the-utility language.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as sufficient bill acknowledgment given customer gave a vague range ($50-300) rather than a clean number, limiting flip material.
coaching_implication: Rep should reflect the number back as the customer's own reason to act later in the call, e.g. tying the appointment to 'getting that bill number down' — never happened.

quote: I can't do it right now. I'll maybe it'll give me some text.
stewart_read: First bill deflection; rep pivots to texting the link but doesn't lock a specific return time.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep should have proposed a specific callback time right here instead of leaving it open.
coaching_implication: Anchor a specific day/time for the bill follow-up immediately, not a vague 'whenever you have a minute.'

quote: Maybe I'll send you later on.
stewart_read: Second deflection touch; rep again accepts vague timing without pinning a return call or appointment.
coaching_implication: This is the second chance to lock a callback time and the rep let it pass again — should have said 'Let's set a specific time I can call you back once you have that.'

quote: Maybe go to another day for them ultimately.
stewart_read: Third and final deflection touch, call ends without any locked date or appointment.
coaching_implication: By the third deflection the rep should have converted to a callback appointment with a named day/time rather than accepting 'around the end of the day' informally.

quote: my neighbor, they got installed solar last week.
stewart_read: Neighbor-influence is a real interest anchor and a natural social-proof hook, but rep never returns to it later in the call.
coaching_implication: Rep could have used the neighbor reference to build urgency/curiosity ('let's see what your numbers look like compared to theirs') — this reason was never reinforced.

quote: did your neighbors get solar with Ion Solar?
stewart_read: Customer directly asks whether the neighbor used Ion — a natural curiosity/social-proof opening the rep does not clearly answer or leverage.
alternative_hypothesis: The transcript here is garbled (repeated 'I don't know' from likely diarization noise), so it's unclear if rep responded at all; may be an audio artifact rather than a rep miss.
coaching_implication: If genuinely unanswered, rep should confirm or redirect ('I can check that for you') to build legitimacy via the neighbor comparison.

quote: I can keep the call super brief for you. I just help get those solar systems created.
stewart_read: Minor scope framing — rep describes their own role in a way that undersells the appointment value ('I just help get those solar systems created') rather than building toward booking a specialist review.
alternative_hypothesis: Could simply be rapport-building shorthand, not a real scope violation since no technical content was given away.
coaching_implication: Frame the call's purpose around getting the customer real savings numbers from a specialist, not around the rep's own limited function.
